edits.value_json: 回 is associated with turning and circular motion, and commonly means “return” or counts an occurrence. Its earliest referent and the relationship between these uses remain uncertain.

回 is treated in one account as a pictograph of a revolving loop; another describes its inner shape as resembling rotation within 囗. A competing analysis proposes that 囘 “whirl” and 回 “around” were originally distinct graphs and words. The depicted object and the relationship between these analyses remain unresolved.
回 is treated as a whole picture associated with circular motion. Shuowen describes an outer 囗 and an inner revolving shape, but this does not establish them as independent components.

字源 describes Shang–Zhou forms as revolving loops, Warring States Qin forms as two enclosed rings, and later forms as following those rings. These are reported form descriptions, not a verified sequence of dated artifacts.

Shuowen describes an outer 囗 enclosing a shape resembling rotation. A competing proposal treats 囘 and 回 as originally distinct graphs and words, with 回 made for “around” and modeled on 圍; their relationship remains unresolved.
Turning or revolving is proposed as an early meaning, but the available literary examples and dictionary accounts do not establish a securely dated earliest attestation.
回 is associated with turning or circular motion and commonly means “return”; it can also count an occurrence. Its earliest referent and the development of these uses remain uncertain.
